name: Oxidative Lymphatic Diffusion Injector
description:
The OLDI-3 is a contact-delivery weapon disguised as a standard medical injector, approximately the size and weight of a thick pen. On skin contact and trigger depression, it delivers a payload of oxidative iron nanoparticle suspension directly through the dermis via high-pressure micro-needle array, bypassing the need for visible puncture or vascular access. The particles enter the lymphatic system and begin a slow oxidative process that progressively degrades lymph node tissue, producing an expanding cascade of immune dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and eventually systemic failure. The process takes between three days and three weeks depending on the payload concentration and the target's biological constitution.

The insidious design intent of the OLDI-3 is temporal dislocation — the weapon is designed to be used in a moment of brief physical contact (a handshake, a crowd brush, a brief struggle) and to produce consequences that emerge long after any connection to that moment can be established. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals developed it under a medical research exemption, ostensibly to study lymphatic drug delivery mechanisms. The weaponized application was, according to company documentation, entirely unintended, a position that has satisfied no investigator who has examined it. The injector contains no moving parts that would register on standard weapons scanners, and the micro-needle array is indistinguishable from a standard dermal patch applicator.

The name 'Rust' describes the slow, inevitable quality of its effect. 'The Long Shake' refers to the handshake delivery method favored by professional operators, and has entered GLMZ's political vocabulary as a term for any arrangement where the consequences of a meeting only become apparent weeks later.
specifications:
delivery method: Contact transdermal, no visible puncture
payload volume: 0.3 mL per injection
onset window: 3-21 days post-delivery
progression rate: Variable by target biology and concentration
injector dimensions: 14cm length, 1.2cm diameter
weight: 38g
payload cartridges: Single-use, 6-cartridge reload block available
scanner profile: Indistinguishable from standard dermal patch applicator on standard weapons scanners
tactical_use: Exclusively an assassination and political destabilization tool. Operators use it in settings where brief physical contact is possible and plausible — social events, negotiations, medical environments, transportation. Professional operators favor the handshake delivery but also use incidental contact in crowds, staged accidents, and posed medical examinations. The weapon's temporal displacement is its primary tactical value: by the time symptoms appear, the delivery moment is days or weeks past, and establishing a chain of custody to the injector is extraordinarily difficult. Countermeasures involve lymphatic screening protocols and blanket nanoparticle filters, but these are expensive and not routinely deployed.
cultural_context: The OLDI-3 has created a specific strain of paranoia in GLMZ's upper political and corporate strata that operators call 'handshake anxiety.' High-value individuals in contested spaces have begun refusing physical contact entirely, conducting all meetings through intermediaries or behind barrier glass. This behavior has in turn become a social signal — someone who will not shake hands is either extremely cautious or has something to hide — which creates its own set of political complications. Among assassination contractors, the OLDI-3 is considered a premium tool, not because it is difficult to use but because its temporal displacement makes attribution nearly impossible, which means the operator's exposure is minimal. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals has never publicly acknowledged the weapon exists.
story_hooks: A city council member is dying of what appears to be accelerated lymphatic failure — three weeks ago they attended a routine negotiation session with six other people, and now the operator has to figure out which of the five surviving attendees shook their hand.

A batch of OLDI-3 cartridges has been stolen from a Lazarus Pharmaceuticals distribution point, but the theft records show the cartridges contained a modified payload — one that works in hours, not weeks, eliminating the weapon's primary advantage and suggesting someone wants bodies found quickly.
An operator wakes up with symptoms consistent with OLDI-3 exposure and has to reconstruct every physical contact from the past three weeks while the clock runs down.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals has quietly developed an antidote — but they are only offering it to clients who can prove they were exposed, which requires admitting they know what the OLDI-3 is and how it works.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, medical-grade injector pen with an almost clinical aesthetic—deliberately engineered to evoke pharmaceutical legitimacy. Its elongated cylindrical form tapers subtly toward the delivery end, where a barely-visible micro-aperture sits flush with the housing. At first glance, indistinguishable from a standard dermal applicator or luxury pen.
physical_description.dimensions: 140mm length, 12mm diameter, delivery head projects 2-3mm from barrel terminus
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light—38g creates an almost negligible heft in the palm, lending it the feel of a premium writing instrument rather than a weapon. The weight is perfectly balanced along its length, designed to rest naturally in a closed fist or nestle invisibly in jacket pockets.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade titanium-aluminum alloy chassis with a medical-grade polymer grip collar
physical_description.finish: Brushed satin finish across the barrel with a subtle gradient—clinical white-silver at the grip transitioning to matte gunmetal at the delivery end. No visible seams or panel lines.
physical_description.color_scheme: Sterile white-silver primary with matte charcoal micro-accents around the trigger mechanism and delivery aperture. Grip collar in soft dove gray.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured medical-grade silicone with barely-perceptible dimpling—designed to prevent slip during 'social contact scenarios.' Feels almost organic against skin.
distinctive_features: Nearly-invisible micro-needle array concealed within the delivery aperture—no protrusion, only a microscopic perforated opening
Flush, pressure-sensitive trigger mechanism requiring deliberate depression—disguised as a standard applicator button
Cartridge-lock collar at the barrel base: single-use indicator, changes color subtly from clear to opaque post-discharge
Minimalist laser-etched serial numbering on the underside of the grip (only visible under direct light inspection)
No manufacturer logos visible on the primary surface—all branding relocated to concealed documentation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Lazarus Compound Operations identifier etched microscopically on the internal cartridge collar; visible only when disassembled. Marketing documentation, if recovered, bears only generic medical device certification marks.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine and sterile—maintained in protective polymer sleeves. Field units show minimal wear; the weapon's assassination-specific use means it spends minimal time in actual combat environments. Storage in climate-controlled cases is standard for black-market operators.
